coverage.why: One firecrawl render of the Austin city page returned edmtrain's entire forward-looking list in a single load -- no 'load more' control or pagination marker appeared anywhere in the rendered markdown, and the list runs to Jun 12 2027 on its own, past our May 31 2027 cutoff. So this is a complete read of everything Edmtrain currently has listed for Austin, not a truncated sample. Events past 2027-05-31 were read but dropped from the output (out of scope). Un-matched venues (0-count rows above) are venues Edmtrain simply has nothing booked at right now, not venues it lacks a page for -- the citywide feed covers all of Austin, there's no per-venue subpage to be missing. (Correction: an earlier draft of this note guessed at genre reasons for the zero-count venues -- that was inference, not something the source stated, so it's been removed. All we actually know is the citywide feed had nothing booked there as of fetch time.)

cityWide.note: Counted every dated event row in the rendered citywide list (all Austin-area venues, not just our 17) with a date between 2026-09-24 and 2026-10-24 inclusive -- 81 of 149 total rows read fell in that window. Note the citywide feed is not electronic-only in practice: alongside club/rave listings (Kingdom, Concourse, Vulcan) it also carried non-electronic bookings like Jungle, Sylvan Esso, and Bonobo -- Edmtrain's own genre toggle (Electronic vs 'Rap, Pop, Rock, Country...') didn't appear to be filtering the version firecrawl rendered.

linkBehavior: The visible 'Buy Tickets' link on every event is edmtrain's own URL (event page + '?get=tickets', e.g. https://edmtrain.com/austin-tx/jungle-world-tour-2026-jungle-489788?get=tickets) -- never a direct ticketer link. Following it once (curl -IL) showed it 302s through an Impact-network affiliate redirector (ticketmaster.evyy.net) and lands on the real ticketer (ticketmaster.com in this case) carrying edmtrain's own affiliate/UTM tags (utm_source=...-EDM+Train+LLC, utm_medium=affiliate). So the destination ticketer is real but only discoverable by following the redirect -- the listing itself never names the ticketer (ticketmaster/axs/etc.) in text, which is why every event below has ticketer: null. A subset of events also print a separate 'StubHub Tickets' link alongside Buy Tickets (flagged in notes) -- that is Edmtrain surfacing StubHub resale inventory for the same show, not a duplicate listing.
